title: Cleverness never found it
hookLine: the restless, clever mind has never found Him (Anand)

cards: People admire the clever ones. The kid who finds the loophole in the rules. The friend who always knows the shortcut.
The person who can argue any side and win. Modern life rewards it: hack your sleep, hack your diet, hack your productivity. There's a life hack for everything.
So it's a little startling when a pauri of Anand Sahib looks straight at cleverness and says, flatly, that it has never once found the One. Not rarely. Never.

teach.b: The pauri opens: ae man chanchal chaturaaee kinai na paaiaa. O restless mind, no one has found him through cleverness. Chanchal means restless, flickering, like a flame in the wind.
Chaturaaee is cleverness, cunning. Kinai na paaiaa: no one has found. Then, in paraphrase: listen, my mind.
This enticing illusion, maya, has led people astray in doubt, and the One who made that enticing illusion is the One who set it in the world. It's the mind again, addressed directly, as in pauri two.
But this time the Guru names the mind's favorite trick. Why would cleverness fail? Because it's a way of getting, and yesterday showed what this tradition says about getting.
Cleverness finds angles, works systems, beats the claw machine.

teach.h: YOU CAN'T OUTSMART THE GAME'S MAKER.
teach.b: But the One isn't a system; you can't outsmart the One who made the game. Guru Nanak says it in the Japji's first pauri too, in paraphrase: you could have a hundred thousand clevernesses, and not one goes with you.
The Gurus aren't against intelligence; the Guru Granth Sahib is full of brilliant poetry and sharp thinking.
They're against cleverness used as a way around surrender. The restless mind keeps thinking there must be a trick. The way in, Anand keeps saying, is love, and grace, and staying.
No trick is needed, and none would work.

how: Many Sikhs recite this pauri as part of the full forty-pauri Anand Sahib in the morning Nitnem; its opening line is often quoted in Sikh teaching against cleverness and pride in spiritual life.

the Japji also says not one cleverness goes with you

games.q: you're the cleverest person you know. you're sure there's a trick to finding God. what does this pauri of Anand say?
o: find the right trick and you'll get there.
O restless mind, no one has found him through cleverness.
only clever people need to try.
games.why: ae man chanchal chaturaaee kinai na paaiaa: no one, ever, has found him through cleverness. the way in is love, grace, and staying.

practice: Notice one plan that's a bit too clever: a way to get someone to do what you want without asking, a shortcut around something you should just face, a strategy for looking good.

Hold it up to the light, then set it down, and picture the plain way instead: asking directly, being seen as you are. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you let it go; if not, notice how much lighter the plain way feels.

wordCard.voice: Chaturaaee, cleverness. Ae man chanchal chaturaaee kinai na paaiaa: O restless mind, no one has ever found the Lord through chaturaaee.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: chaturaaee, cleverness or cunning; Anand says no one has found the Lord through it.

carryVoice: Your line: not by cleverness. This is one door that doesn't open to a trick. Until tomorrow.
